capability: NIST CORR-DATA (2017 doi:10.18434/M3TH4R) marine steel corrosion baseline. Extracts 588 numeric corrosion rate records from 30 unique source documents in seawater, sodium chloride, and marine atmospheric environments across 5 coating-substrate material groups (carbon steel, stainless, copper, aluminum, nickel alloys). Fits a Ridge regression baseline on log10(mm/yr) target with environment + material-group one-hot + temperature + log-concentration + log-duration features, evaluated with Leave-One-Source-Document-Out CV. Baseline beats per-material-group-median NULL by +0.0475 log10 units. Documents uncoated-substrate seawater corrosion rates that any coating claim must reduce. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.
dataset_fixture_note: NIST CORR-DATA Database v2017 (doi:10.18434/M3TH4R). Public data. 24,721 total records; 588 used after marine + material-group + numeric-rate filtering.

metrics.name: n_records_at_least_300
metrics.note: n_records = 588 marine records (Seawater / Sodium Chloride / Atmospheric Environments) after filtering for numeric mm/yr rate, strictly-positive rate (for log target), and coating-substrate material groups (Carbon and alloy steels, Stainless steels, Copper/Aluminum/Nickel alloys). Adequate scale for a defensible baseline.

metrics.name: n_source_documents_at_least_10
metrics.note: n_source_documents = 30 unique source-document references (Reference # column) → Leave-One-Source-Document-Out CV uses 30 folds, protecting against per-study methodology bias.

metrics.name: n_environments_at_least_3
metrics.note: n_environments = 3. Environments in scope: ['Atmospheric Environments', 'Seawater', 'Sodium Chloride']. All three marine-relevant environment classes from NIST CORR-DATA.

metrics.name: n_material_groups_at_least_3
metrics.note: n_material_groups = 5. Material groups in scope: ['Aluminum and alloys', 'Carbon and alloy steels', 'Copper and alloys', 'Nickel and alloys', 'Stainless steels'].

metrics.name: ridge_beats_null_baseline_on_LOSD_CV
metrics.note: Ridge (α=0.01, environment × material_group one-hot + temperature + log-concentration + log-duration) achieves LOSD-CV MAE(log10 rate) = 0.6331 vs NULL (per-material-group median log10 rate) MAE = 0.6806. Reduction = +0.0475 log10 units (7.0% relative improvement). MODEST but real: adding environment + numeric-condition features beats naive material-group-median prediction.

metrics.name: MAE_log10_rate_below_1_0
metrics.note: LOSD-CV MAE(log10) = 0.6331 < 1.0 log10 unit (within a factor of 10 in linear rate). Corrosion rates in the filtered marine subset span 5.9 orders of magnitude, so predicting to within a factor of 4.3 is a defensible baseline for public data.

metrics.name: seawater_carbon_steel_baseline_documented
metrics.note: Uncoated carbon steel in seawater: median = 0.1000 mm/yr, 25-75th percentile = [0.0800, 0.1500] mm/yr (n = 44 records). THIS IS THE REFERENCE RATE ANY MARINE ANTI-CORROSION COATING CLAIM MUST BEAT.

metrics.name: seawater_stainless_baseline_documented
metrics.note: Uncoated stainless steel in seawater: median = 0.0120 mm/yr. Stainless is inherently corrosion-resistant; the median rate here is much lower than carbon steel, so 'coating on stainless' claims must be assessed against a lower baseline.

population: 588 NIST CORR-DATA records after filtering: Environment ∈ {Seawater, Sodium Chloride, Atmospheric Environments}; Material Group ∈ {Carbon and alloy steels, Stainless steels, Copper/Aluminum/Nickel alloys}; numeric mm/yr rate > 0. Spans 30 unique source documents (Reference # column, gold-standard for guarding against per-study methodology bias).
split_methodology: Leave-One-Source-Document-Out CV (30 folds). Each fold trains on records from 29 source documents and predicts on the held-out document's records. Ridge fit at 5 alpha values [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 100.0]; best alpha selected by lowest CV MAE(log10 rate). Reproducible under seed=0.
